content.text: Currently app/ and landing/ designs different from the designs that are in the claude design collections. Is there a way to transfer over this implementation into the claude design collections?

Yes. Claude Design has a sync path for this: the **`/design-sync`** command. It takes a local component library and pushes it into one of your claude.ai/design design-system projects. It works one component at a time and never replaces the whole project. For each component it builds a preview card (tokens, type, colors, buttons and so on), compares that against what's already in the project, and shows you the exact list of files it will write or delete before uploading anything.

Two things are in the way right now:

1. **The Claude Design connection failed in this session.** api.anthropic.com rejected the login with a 403, which usually means your current login token doesn't include Claude Design access. Run `/design-login` from an interactive `claude` terminal to fix it.
2. **`/design-sync` has to be started by you.** I can't launch that sync myself, and `/design-sync` isn't in this session's command list. So run it from a terminal session where Claude Design is connected, after step 1.

To get a cleaner result, run it once for each source:
- **`landing/`** as one design-system project, or as a "Brand" group inside a shared one.
- **`frontend/`** (the app) as the product UI kit.

Since your last commit aligned the color tokens between the two, one shared project with separate groups for brand/landing and app components would likely work well. Each sync shows you what already exists in the project, so you can choose to overwrite or keep the old designs one component at a time.

If you'd rather not use the sync, I can build a standalone design-system page from the current tokens and components (colors, type, buttons, cards, the state colors) and publish it as an Artifact. You can then bring it into Claude Design by hand.

They're `position: fixed` overlays; the screenshots are correct. - `[RENDER_THIN] FighterOverlay`: "variants render identically". content.text:
The designs differ because the sync left gaps in what Claude Design can see. Wherever a card is a placeholder or a piece wasn't uploaded at all, Claude Design invents its own version. I checked this from the local sync output in `ds-bundle/` and `.design-sync/`, not from the project itself, because this session has no design access.

**1. 8 components went up as blank placeholder cards.** Their previews crashed because the sync didn't pass them the data they need (from `ds-bundle/.render-check.json`):
- FightReport, FightBreakdown, Momentum, RecentForm: most of the Player screen
- AnnotateStage, VideoPlayer: the Annotate screen
- ProvenanceLine, RoundsCheck

Claude Design has never seen what these look like, so it improvises them.

**2. Components that load data from the backend were left out on purpose.** That includes Header, FightLedger, UploadDialog, EventTable and EventReview (listed in `.design-sync/NOTES.md`). Every design therefore invents its own navigation bar and fight list.

**3. No full screens and no landing page were uploaded.** Only separate components went up, plus the logo pieces from `landing/`. The landing page's sections (hero, features, waitlist) aren't in the design system. Whole screens get assembled by Claude Design from the individual pieces, so their layouts won't match yours.

**4. Two things I couldn't check:**
- Designs made before the sync keep their old look. Updating the design system doesn't change them, so they need to be regenerated.
- The sync only adds files and never deletes any. If the project had older hand-made token or README files, they're probably still there and can contradict the new ones. Re-running `/design-sync` will show you the remote file list.

The fix is mostly local: write preview files with sample data for the 8 crashed components, plus versions of Header and FightLedger that use sample data instead of the backend. You then re-run `/design-sync` to upload them.
Issue is that designs also differed away from the Claude designs, the real implementation also changed some stuff. I want to update that stuff as well
